source.title: EAP-GP: Mitigating Saturation Effect in Gradient-based Automated Circuit Identification
source.authors: Lin Zhang; Wen-Shuo Dong; Zhuoran Zhang; Shu Yang; Lijie Hu; Ninghao Liu; Pan Zhou; Di Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant IOI table values are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates alternative gradient-based circuit-identification methods on IOI and reports circuit faithfulness and overlap with manually identified circuits. This is a conceptual test of method sensitivity, not a reproduction of the original head-level interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test the original 26-head, 7-class circuit or the stated head roles. Its IOI results concern circuits identified by EAP, EAP-IG, and EAP-GP, evaluated by normalized faithfulness; its IOI manual-overlap results are described partly in text and shown in a figure. It does not report results on backup-head ablation, reuse across tasks, or prompt variants. Runtime comparisons do not bear on the claim and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper proposing EAP-GP. Its IOI results are normalized faithfulness scores for circuits picked by its own method versus EAP and EAP-IG, which is method benchmarking. The manually found IOI circuit serves only as ground truth for scoring its method, shown as figure-only precision-recall curves. The paper does not test whether the 26-head circuit holds or whether its faithfulness depends on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that EAP-IG's straight-line path suffers saturation effects. They report that EAP-GP's adaptive GradPath improves circuit faithfulness, by up to 17.7%, across six tasks and three GPT-2 sizes. They say its precision/recall against manual circuits is comparable to or better than prior methods, while noting the IOI comparison may be flawed because of ambiguous MLP roles.
record.recipe_differences: This study evaluates automated edge-attribution circuit identification methods (EAP, EAP-IG, and proposed EAP-GP), rather than testing the original study's proposed 26-head circuit and its head-level roles. It varies gradient integration paths and evaluates extracted circuits at specified edge sparsities.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported IOI NFS changes with attribution method and edge sparsity. In an additional EAP-GP ablation, the number of integration steps is varied from k=3 to 20 and the text reports that more sparsity reduction or increasing steps beyond k=5 can lower faithfulness. Prompt distribution and evaluation metric are not varied for IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: Precision-recall curves of EAP, EAP-IG and EAP-GP circuits against the manual IOI circuit show 'similar trends'. The authors call the assessment possibly flawed because of the MLPs' ambiguous role.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-based edge attribution recovers only part of the manual IOI circuit at high sparsity (edge recall in Figure 5 plotted only up to about 0.4).

record.problems: The manual-circuit precision-recall values for IOI are only plotted and are not given numerically in the text. The authors note possible ambiguity in the MLP roles of the manually identified IOI circuit. The IOI faithfulness results evaluate automatically selected circuits, not the original 26-head circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI rows were omitted. The paper's GPT-2 Medium and GPT-2 XL results concern circuits identified by these methods, but do not assess whether the original circuit's head classes and roles persist. Runtime values were excluded because they do not measure the claim's behavior or circuit faithfulness.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes, head roles, and faithfulness/completeness/minimality of the original circuit.
Head classes and roles in GPT-2 Medium/XL (only method NFS is reported there), and component reuse.
Whether automated methods recover essentially the same heads and roles. The PR curves are figure-only and framed as scoring the methods.
Effect of ablation, metric or prompt distribution on the original circuit's faithfulness.

missing.what: Readable precision/recall values for IOI node and edge overlap with the manual circuit, if extractable from the plot.
missing.versions: V4 (only if later reclassified as a test)

record.verdict_notes: I reclassify the study from tests/T2 to T4. All IOI results score automatically found circuits from the authors' own method and its baselines, so they say nothing about whether the original circuit holds. The V4 and V5 labels in the record are removed. The V5 'supports' label in particular rested on method-comparison NFS, not on evaluation-choice sensitivity of the IOI circuit.

versions.untested_parts: The specified 26 attention heads, 7 classes, head roles, and the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, and minimality are not tested.
No main name-mover ablation or self-repair/backup-head test.
The paper evaluates IOI circuits in GPT-2 Medium and GPT-2 XL, but does not test whether the original head classes and roles are preserved, or whether components are reused for other tasks.
It compares EAP, EAP-IG, and EAP-GP and reports IOI overlap with manual circuits. It does not test other ablation types or whether changing the metric recovers the same circuit.
It varies attribution method, edge sparsity, and EAP-GP step count and reports IOI faithfulness. It does not vary ablation type, evaluation metric, or prompt distribution.
No comparison of IOI name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

relation.reason: Manual-circuit overlap scores method retrieval, while normalized faithfulness evaluates each method's selected circuits rather than the original 26-head circuit.

tranche.reason: The study benchmarks circuit-identification methods and uses the manual IOI circuit as ground truth; it does not independently test its head classes, roles or claimed criteria.

source_check.notes: These rows report method benchmarks and should not serve as claim evidence. IOI normalization uses clean/corrupted logit-difference baselines 3.80/0.03; the authors caution that ambiguous MLP membership weakens the manual-overlap comparison.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI precision-recall comparison across EAP, EAP-IG, and EAP-GP
reader_labels.reason: The authors report similar overall node and edge precision-recall trends among the three methods, although the figure does not provide readable exact values (ioi-pr-node-eap, ioi-pr-edge-eap, ioi-pr-node-ig, ioi-pr-edge-ig, ioi-pr-node-gp, ioi-pr-edge-gp).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: EAP-GP IOI precision-recall curves, especially at lower recall
reader_labels.reason: The text says EAP-GP initially performs worse, with only a slight improvement as recall increases; the authors also caution that manual IOI circuit overlap may be affected by ambiguity about MLP roles (ioi-pr-node-gp, ioi-pr-edge-gp).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small IOI circuits across tested attribution methods and edge sparsities
reader_labels.reason: NFS varies substantially with method and sparsity, and even the reported 80.08% at 97.50% sparsity is below full normalized faithfulness (all ioi-s-* rows).
